documents.title: Routine follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SUBJECTIVE
Routine follow-up. Last cardiology contact was the 10/2024 phone follow-up after the July 2024 visit (positive repeat stress test, nitroglycerin started). He reports no new symptoms: angina only with stairs, same as the past year, relieved by rest or one nitro, no rest pain. Taking metformin, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin every day; nitro and sildenafil as needed and never within a day of each other. Fasting today.

He picked up a flyer in our waiting room for a research study of a new cholesterol-lowering medicine and asks whether he could join and what it involves.

OBJECTIVE
BP 138/86 (scale out of service this morning - no weight today).
Comfortable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet unchanged: intact skin, reduced monofilament, diminished pulses.
Fasting labs drawn.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Interest in clinical trial - We talked through how a trial like this works. Participants are assigned at random, by computer, to the study medicine or a placebo (an inactive pill that looks the same); neither he nor I choose, and usually neither he nor the study staff know which one he is getting until the study ends. That is how the study can tell whether the drug itself works. Taking part is voluntary, he can stop at any time, and his regular care here continues either way. The study team, not us, decides who qualifies. Gave him the study information sheet and coordinator contact from the flyer; he will read it and call them if he wants to go forward.
2. Stable angina - stable pattern; aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, NTG prn. Due for his yearly cardiology visit; gave him their number to book.
3. T2DM with CKD 1 and neuropathy - A1c and BMP today.
4. HTN - amlodipine 5.
5. Hyperlipidemia - lipid panel today; atorvastatin 20.
6. PAD, ED - stable.

RTC 6 months.

Addendum 1/13: A1c 7.2%. Fasting glucose 154. Lipids: TC 210, LDL 130, HDL 45, TG 250. Creatinine 0.8, eGFR 99.

documents.title: January results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Gary,
Your fasting labs from Monday: A1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 154. Kidney function normal. Cholesterol: total 210, LDL 130, HDL 45, triglycerides 250 - close to your last few panels.
No changes to your medicines. If you do contact the study team, let me know what they say; I'm happy to send them any records they need with your permission.

documents.title: Refill: nitroglycerin, sildenafil
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Mail-order requests: nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL #25 (refills used up) and sildenafil 50 mg (urology Rx expired). Pended both to PCP.
PCP: nitroglycerin sent #25 x 2 refills. Sildenafil 50 mg #6 sent x 3 refills, same sig, with "do not take within 24 hours of nitroglycerin" added to the directions.

documents.title: DM follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six-month follow-up. No new symptoms. Exertional chest pressure unchanged and infrequent, nitro as needed, sits when he takes it. Feet numb, no wounds. Eye exam 6/19: no retinopathy. Medications taken daily, no side effects.

O: BP 127/82, HR 78, SpO2 98%, wt 87.2 kg (BMI 27.5).
Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Foot exam: dry skin, metatarsal calluses, no ulcer, protective sensation reduced, pulses diminished.

A/P:
- T2DM w/ CKD 1, neuropathy: A1c, BMP, UACR today.
- HTN: amlodipine 5.
- Stable angina, PAD: no change.
- Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 20.
RTC 3 months.

Addendum 7/16: A1c 7.3%, UACR 46, eGFR 95.
